summary: Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held posts attested in 2007 as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University.

Mikisaburo Mori (1909–1986) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932). He held academic posts at Osaka University (~1950–1973) and Bukkyo University (~1973–1984).

Ming Mei works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (BA 1966–1974) and UCLA (PhD 1974–1979 under Kenneth Kuan Sheng Ch'en and Robert C. Epp), later serving as professor at HKU (~1976–2008).
Mingyu Fu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Shi Huifeng (attested 2013).

Minonori Nishimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Taisho University (~1970–1976), studying under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, and later served as an associate professor there (~1993) and researcher at Sanko Research Institute (attested 2002).

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) specialized in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard University, and served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1991), president of ICPEB (1996–2006), and director of IIBS (~1997–2011).

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1946–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1963). He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1966 to 1994.
Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1868–1870). He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1899) and Harvard University (~1899–1907).

Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies under Masatoshi Nagatomi, studied with Robert A. F. Thurman, and was mentored by B. N. Mukherjee during postdoctoral work.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, later holding professorships at the University of Bucharest, University of Paris, and University of Chicago.

Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) was a scholar in Tibetology. She served as Chargé de Recherche at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1961–1993) and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at the University of Western Australia and UNSW.

Miriam Levering (1943–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).
Mirjan Damaška (1931–2023) studied at the University of Ljubljana (~1959–1960) and served on the faculty at Yale Law School from approximately 1976 to 2023.

Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942) and worked in Sinology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Kitakyushu (~1950–1969), University of Tokyo (~1969–1970), Kyoto University (~1970–1982), and Kansai University (~1982–1989).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi (1944–) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held an academic post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saigusa (1923–2010) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950), he served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~1974–1987) and held a post at Kokugakuin University (~1987–1994).

Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1931–1934). He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1949–1982) and at Shitennoji University (attested 1976).
